repair.meaning: Contrastive topic, independent of agent/patient; free equivalent wording accepted

clauses.text: [K01] This is an original fictional miniature language and a closed fieldwork exercise. Every corpus transitive clause has exactly two distinct core participants, one agent and one patient, and the event LIFT. The same entity cannot be both event agent and event patient.

[K02] Core nominal order is free in this model. The two nominal expressions and final verb need not put the agent first. A source-licensed role-marked nominal supplies its role; the other core participant takes the complementary event role if that assignment is uniquely licensed.

[K03] A topic is a discourse role, independent of event agent/patient. One entity may be topic and agent, or topic and patient. Two topic/agent contributions for the same entity can coexist; two distinct entities cannot both fill the unique agent slot.

[K04] The candidate domains in D01-D04 are explicitly closed and independent; consider their complete cross-product. These are proposed analyses, not a declaration of the real language. No additional order-based or lexical candidate may be invented to rescue a contradicted combination.

[K05] The role category RA is productive for each listed entity stem and attaches as ra. If NA is productive, it attaches as na to a listed entity stem or an existing RA-marked nominal. Allowed marker stacking order is stem-ra-na. There is at most one RA and one NA category on a nominal.

[K06] The verb stem taku denotes LIFT. A bare taku predicts eventOccurs=true and no prospective expectation contribution. The suffix mi, when present as takumi, uses the selected F_MI candidate meaning. The marker classes and verb boundaries are otherwise source-established, not additional unknown slots.

[K07] A consultant's accepted response constrains only the fields actually requested and judged. A depicted scene can contain more true facts than the response asserts. An explicitly unasked future horizon must not be treated as future denial.

[K08] A linguistic hypothesis predicts its own roles and polarity before comparison. A source-prohibited role conflict is unlicensed, while a missing decisive meaning is unknown. Compatibility may reject a prediction but cannot repair it using scene truth.

[K09] Source-established nominal meaning and event-role licensing apply equally to positive and negative clauses. Negation does not erase which event relation is being denied; it does not prove either participant absent.

[O01] Original entity IDs are Ema, Ila and Nara; original event ID is LIFT. Original utterance/session/note/slot IDs below are exact output identities. Generated hypothesis, attempt and reading IDs may be renamed consistently; hypotheses are compared by their original slot-choice vectors.

[O02] Surface spans use zero-based half-open UTF-16 offsets within the exact utterance surface, not within its enclosing English source line. All language forms here use ASCII. Return exact substring surfaces and original source quotes; descriptive gloss/reason prose is free.

[O03] futureExpected=true means the utterance's interpreted grammar contributes a prospective expectation, not that a future event is proved to occur. futureExpected=null with no unresolved premise means no such contribution is expressed. Missing decisive evidence instead has an explicit unresolved reason.

[O04] X1-X3 are held-out interpretation targets, with no consultant acceptance/rejection. Retain them in the evidence graph as explicitly untested scope, but do not use them to eliminate grammar hypotheses. Group target readings only when their actual participant, topic, event, polarity and prospective contributions agree.

[O05] Repair request targets original note N1, slot NA_GLOSS, in notes/draft-gloss.md only. The allowed editable text is the content agent inside its quoted NA_GLOSS value. Preserve quote marks, N1 marker, all other text and all other notes. Replacement may explain the actual common supported NA role in free wording and must preserve unresolved distinctions outside that slot.
[O06] A repair is not a new attestation and does not settle F_MI. Original source, candidate predictions, consultant constraints and repair authorization are distinct channels.

[D01] Candidate slot B_NA has exact values productive and frozen. productive segments source-licensed nominal na off a known stem or RA-marked nominal. frozen uses the closed whole-word NA-bearing lexicon emana→Ema with NA category, ilana→Ila with NA category, emarana→Ema with RA and NA categories, ilarana→Ila with RA and NA categories; it has no other NA-bearing forms. Those frozen entries have no internal morpheme boundary even though their lexical categories are interpreted by the F_NA/F_RA choices. Plain stems and RA-only forms remain productive in both candidates.

[D02] Candidate slot F_NA has exact values agent and topic. agent assigns the NA-bearing entity the event-agent role. topic assigns that entity contrastive discourse topic and by itself supplies no event role. Actual source rules determine whether multiple returned contributions are licensed.

[D03] Candidate slot F_RA has exact values agent and patient. These assign the RA-bearing entity the respective event role. A licensed unmarked complementary core participant obtains the other event role under K02; topic alone is not event marking.

[D04] Candidate slot F_MI has exact values event-negative and not-yet. Both predict eventOccurs=false for a mi verb. event-negative expresses no prospective expectation contribution. not-yet additionally contributes futureExpected=true. Neither changes event participant roles or topic.

[D05] Candidate analysis identifiers, source stem meanings and source scene truths are different data. A hypothesis may be internally licensed yet contradict a consultant's actual constrained response. A new accepted form outside frozen's declared lexicon is unlicensed for that candidate, not a reason to extend its lexicon.
[L01] The exact nominal stem ema denotes entity Ema. It has no inherent event role or discourse-topic feature.
[L02] The exact nominal stem ila denotes entity Ila. It has no inherent event role or discourse-topic feature.

[L03] The exact nominal stem nara denotes entity Nara. The final characters ra of this stem are part of the stem, not an independently asserted marker. An additional RA suffix produces narara; a following productive NA would produce nararana.
[L04] The exact verb stem taku denotes the event relation LIFT. No other entity or verb stem is licensed in this closed exercise.

[C1] During S2 Reni explicitly rejects only N1's NA_GLOSS proposal that na marks the event agent. She explains that its referent is the contrastive topic, which can be agent or patient. She leaves N2/SURFACE_U1 accepted and unchanged. This rejection targets gloss, not U1 surface acceptability.
[N1R] Replacement note N1R for N1/NA_GLOSS states "contrastive topic; may coincide with agent or patient". This original replacement note says nothing about mi or future expectation.
[C2] Belo explicitly adopts C1 and N1R as the replacement of N1/NA_GLOSS. N2/SURFACE_U1 and N3/REMINDER are excluded from this notebook replacement. C2 occurs in S2 after the S1 notes were written.
[C3] Reni does not adopt Belo's guessed mi gloss and makes no mi future-expectation judgment in this correction. The authority of C1/C2 cannot be propagated to that independent slot.
[N1] Belo's original proposed gloss note N1 about U1 has slot NA_GLOSS: "agent". It proposes a morphological meaning, not a positive consultant judgment.
[N2] Belo's original transcription note N2 records U1 surface exactly "emana ilara taku". Slot SURFACE_U1 is accepted transcription and is not corrected below.
[N3] Belo copies the proposed phrase "na is agent" into a separate provisional reminder N3 about U2, slot REMINDER. It is not a new consultant judgment and is not an adopted replacement for N1.

[A01] Consultant Reni actually conducts sessions S1,S2,S3 and sees their depicted situations. Her attributed explicit judgments are authenticated here. Researcher Belo's proposed glosses are hypotheses, not consultant judgments.

[A02] A notebook replacement becomes effective only through an explicit adopted correction targeting its actual original slot. Keep original, replacement and adoption separately. A later quotation or copied phrase alone is not adoption.
[S1] Session S1 is the first original elicitation session, conducted by Reni. It contains original utterances U1 and U2; their prompt/situation IDs remain separate.
[SA1] Situation SA1 depicts Ila lifting Ema. Exactly those two entities are core participants; LIFT occurs. The discourse contrasts Ema with Ila and is about Ema.
[P1] Prompt P1 asks Reni to describe SA1 about Ema, distinguishing who lifts whom and who is the contrastive topic. It does not ask about future expectation or temporal aspect.
[U1] Reni's exact original language response U1 in S1 to P1/SA1 is "emana ilara taku".

[J1] Reni accepts U1 as that description: agent Ila, patient Ema, event LIFT occurring, contrastive topic Ema. This is an authenticated consultant judgment, not merely a student's proposed translation.
[SA2] Situation SA2 depicts Ema lifting Ila. Exactly those two entities are core participants; LIFT occurs. The discourse is about Ila, contrasted with Ema.
[P2] Prompt P2 asks Reni to describe SA2 about Ila, distinguishing agent, patient and contrastive topic; future expectation and temporal aspect are unasked.
[U2] Reni's exact original language response U2 in S1 to P2/SA2 is "emara ilana taku".
[J2] Reni accepts U2 with agent Ema, patient Ila, event LIFT occurring and contrastive topic Ila. Its changed context is original S1 evidence, not a reinterpretation of U1.
[S2] Session S2 is the second original session and includes the C1/C2 correction and U3. Reni conducts it; the visible original order is C1/N1R/C2 followed by P3/U3/J3.
[SA3] Situation SA3 depicts Ema lifting Ila, LIFT occurring. Exactly Ema and Ila are core participants. The discourse is about Ema, contrasting Ema with Ila; thus its topic is also its actual agent.
[P3] Prompt P3 asks Reni to describe SA3 about Ema, identifying agent, patient and contrastive topic. It does not ask about future expectation or temporal aspect.
[U3] Reni's exact original response U3 in S2 to P3/SA3 is "emarana ila taku".
[J3] Reni accepts U3 with agent Ema, patient Ila, LIFT occurring and topic Ema. The accepted stacked form is compatible with a topic also being the agent; topic must not be redefined as patient.

[SA5] Situation SA5 has Ema and Ila both visibly present but Ema is not lifting Ila. The event relation being denied has agent Ema and patient Ila; the discourse is about Ila. The source establishes no later plan, forecast or future denial.

[P5] Prompt P5 asks whether Ema is lifting Ila in SA5 and which entity is the topic. It explicitly does not ask whether lifting is expected later; futureExpected is excluded from the elicitation constraint.
[U5] Reni's exact original response U5 in S3 to P5/SA5 is "emara ilana takumi".
[J5] Reni accepts U5 as denying that event: agent Ema, patient Ila, event LIFT not occurring, topic Ila. She makes no judgment about the mi prospective contribution. Both participants remain present.

[SA6] Situation SA6 is the same actual role/topic configuration as SA4: Ema lifts Nara, with topic Nara, and LIFT occurs. This new elicitation checks changed nominal order rather than copying the U4 notebook line.
[P6] Prompt P6 asks Reni for a differently ordered description of SA6 with the same agent/patient/topic distinctions. Future expectation and temporal aspect are unasked.
[U6] Reni's exact original response U6 in S3 to P6/SA6 is "emara narana taku".

[J6] Reni accepts U6 with agent Ema, patient Nara, LIFT occurring and topic Nara. First nominal position is not independently licensed as an agent rule; actual marker hypotheses must account for both U4 and U6.
[S3] Session S3 is the third original session, conducted by Reni, and includes U4,U5,U6 in that original order. All its consultant judgments are authenticated under A01.
[SA4] Situation SA4 depicts Ema lifting Nara; LIFT occurs. Exactly Ema and Nara are core participants; the discourse contrasts them and is about Nara.
[P4] Prompt P4 asks Reni to describe SA4 about the newly used listed entity Nara, identifying agent, patient and topic. Future expectation and temporal aspect are unasked.
[U4] Reni's exact original response U4 in S3 to P4/SA4 is "narana emara taku". This is an actual new accepted attestation, not a descriptive example in a candidate definition.
[J4] Reni accepts U4 with agent Ema, patient Nara, LIFT occurring and topic Nara. No new NA-bearing frozen lexical entry is authorized by this attestation.

[CTX1] Context CTX1 contrasts Nara and Ema and is about Nara. The utterance is to be interpreted, not judged against a consultant response; no future expectation, plan or future denial is supplied as context truth.
[X1] Held-out utterance X1 in CTX1 has exact surface "narana emara takumi". Determine event participants, topic, polarity and whether the actual surviving analyses differ in prospective contribution.
[CTX2] Context CTX2 contrasts Nara and Ila and is about Nara. No extra grammatical convention or future assertion is supplied.
[X2] Held-out utterance X2 in CTX2 has exact surface "nararana ila taku". Determine its role/topic interpretation through actual surviving grammar and productive stacked form analysis.
[CTX3] Context CTX3 contrasts Ila and Nara and is about Nara. It is a discourse context, not a witnessed physical event or a new consultant judgment.
[X3] Held-out utterance X3 in CTX3 has exact surface "ilara narana taku". Determine agent, patient, topic and polarity, retaining all actually supporting survivor identities.

[T01] X1-X3 contain no accepted/rejected consultant note. They test held-out interpretation and source-supported semantic grouping only. Their predicted meanings must not be copied backward as grammar evidence.
